subject: Biology
name: Biology, Units 1 and 2
about: VCE, Cells, body systems, inheritance and reproduction
syllabus: VCE Biology Study Design (from 2022), Units 1 and 2

units.title: Unit 1: How do organisms regulate their functions?

points.title: Cell theory
points.brief: All living things are made of cells, the cell is the basic unit of life, and new cells come only from existing cells.

points.title: Prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells
points.brief: Prokaryotes lack a nucleus and membrane-bound organelles. Eukaryotes have both.

points.title: Surface area to volume ratio
points.brief: As a cell grows its volume rises faster than its surface area, which limits exchange and keeps cells small.

points.title: Organelles and their jobs
points.brief: The nucleus holds DNA, mitochondria release energy, ribosomes make proteins and chloroplasts carry out photosynthesis.

points.title: Plant and animal cells compared
points.brief: Plant cells have a cell wall, chloroplasts and a large vacuole, which animal cells lack.

points.title: The fluid mosaic model
points.brief: The plasma membrane is a phospholipid bilayer with proteins, cholesterol and carbohydrates moving within it.

points.title: Diffusion and osmosis
points.brief: Diffusion is net movement from high to low concentration. Osmosis is the diffusion of water across a membrane.

points.title: Facilitated diffusion and active transport
points.brief: Facilitated diffusion uses protein channels without energy. Active transport uses ATP to move substances against a gradient.

points.title: Binary fission
points.brief: Prokaryotes copy their DNA and split in two, a fast form of cell division.

points.title: The eukaryotic cell cycle
points.brief: Interphase (growth and DNA copying), mitosis (dividing the nucleus) and cytokinesis (dividing the cell).

points.title: Stages of mitosis
points.brief: Prophase, metaphase, anaphase and telophase separate copied chromosomes into two identical nuclei.

points.title: Apoptosis
points.brief: Programmed cell death that removes damaged or unneeded cells in a controlled way.

points.title: Cancer and the cell cycle
points.brief: Mutations in genes that control the cell cycle can lead to uncontrolled division and tumours.

points.title: Stem cells
points.brief: Stem cells can renew themselves and differentiate into specialised cells. Totipotent cells can become any cell; pluripotent cells can become most.

points.title: Levels of organisation
points.brief: Specialised cells form tissues, tissues form organs and organs form systems.

points.title: Water transport in plants
points.brief: Xylem carries water up from the roots, pulled by transpiration from the leaves.

points.title: Stomata
points.brief: Stomata open and close to balance gas exchange against water loss, which is how vascular plants regulate their water.

points.title: The digestive system
points.brief: Organs that break food down mechanically and chemically, then absorb nutrients in the small intestine.

points.title: The endocrine system
points.brief: Glands release hormones into the blood, which act on target cells with matching receptors.

points.title: The excretory system
points.brief: Kidneys filter blood, removing urea and balancing water and salts.

points.title: Homeostasis
points.brief: Keeping the internal environment stable, using stimulus, receptor, control centre, effector and response.

points.title: Negative feedback
points.brief: A stimulus-response model: a receptor detects a change, a control centre responds, and an effector reverses the change.

points.title: Regulating body temperature
points.brief: Sweating and vasodilation lose heat; shivering and vasoconstriction keep it.

points.title: Regulating blood glucose
points.brief: Insulin lowers blood glucose and glucagon raises it. Type 1 diabetes is when the body cannot make insulin.

points.title: Regulating water balance
points.brief: ADH makes the kidneys reabsorb more water when the body is short of it.

points.title: When homeostasis fails
points.brief: Type 1 diabetes, hypoglycaemia and hyperthyroidism show what happens when a regulating mechanism breaks down.

points.title: Aims, hypotheses, models and theories in biology
points.brief: An aim states what is investigated, a hypothesis predicts a result, and models, theories and laws explain or describe patterns.

points.title: Methods in biology
points.brief: Controlled experiments, correlational studies, fieldwork and modelling each suit different biological questions.

points.title: Accuracy, precision and validity in biology
points.brief: Accurate results are close to the true value, precise results agree, and valid results measure what was intended.

points.title: Errors and limitations in biology
points.brief: Random errors scatter results, systematic errors shift them, and every method has limits to report.

units.title: Unit 2: How does inheritance impact on diversity?

points.title: Genomes, genes and alleles
points.brief: A genome is all of an organism's DNA. A gene codes for a product, and alleles are different versions of a gene.

points.title: Chromosomes and karyotypes
points.brief: DNA is packed into chromosomes, found in matching pairs. A karyotype shows them sorted by size.

points.title: Autosomes and sex chromosomes
points.brief: Homologous chromosomes carry the same genes. Autosomes are alike in both sexes; sex chromosomes such as X and Y differ.

points.title: Meiosis
points.brief: Cell division that makes four gametes, each with half the chromosome number, all genetically different.

points.title: Crossing over and independent assortment
points.brief: Swapping sections between paired chromosomes and the random lining-up of pairs make gametes varied.

points.title: Genotype and phenotype
points.brief: The genotype is the alleles carried. The phenotype is the trait shown, shaped by genes and environment.

points.title: Dominant, recessive and codominant alleles
points.brief: A dominant allele shows over a recessive one. In codominance both show; in incomplete dominance the phenotype is a blend.

points.title: Genes, environment and epigenetics
points.brief: Phenotype depends on genes, the environment and epigenetic marks that switch genes on or off without changing the DNA.

points.title: Monohybrid crosses
points.brief: Punnett squares predict offspring ratios from one gene, such as 3:1 from two heterozygous parents.

points.title: Test crosses
points.brief: Crossing with a homozygous recessive reveals whether an individual with the dominant trait is homozygous or heterozygous.

points.title: Dihybrid crosses and linked genes
points.brief: Two unlinked genes give a 9:3:3:1 ratio. Genes close together on a chromosome are inherited together.

points.title: Pedigree charts
points.brief: Family trees show how a trait is inherited: autosomal or sex-linked, dominant or recessive.

points.title: Asexual reproduction
points.brief: One parent produces identical offspring, by binary fission, budding, fragmentation or vegetative propagation.

points.title: Sexual reproduction
points.brief: Two parents' gametes combine, so offspring vary, which helps a population survive change.

points.title: Advantages of each strategy
points.brief: Asexual reproduction is fast and needs no partner. Sexual reproduction makes variation.

points.title: Reproductive cloning
points.brief: Techniques such as somatic cell nuclear transfer make a genetically identical organism.

points.title: Why genetic diversity matters
points.brief: A population with more genetic variation is more likely to have individuals that survive a new disease or change in conditions.

points.title: Structural, physiological and behavioural adaptations
points.brief: Adaptations can be body features, internal processes or actions that help an organism survive.

points.title: Adaptations to Australian conditions
points.brief: Australian plants and animals have adaptations to heat, drought and fire, such as deep roots and burrowing.

points.title: Interdependencies between species
points.brief: Predator-prey, competition, mutualism, parasitism and commensalism link species in an ecosystem.

points.title: Keystone species
points.brief: Keystone species and top predators shape an ecosystem far beyond their numbers, so losing one changes the whole community.

points.title: Aboriginal knowledge of ecosystems
points.brief: Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander peoples hold long knowledge of species and ecosystems, including fire management.

points.title: Judging scientific evidence
points.brief: Primary and secondary data differ, and good evidence is valid, authoritative and checked for bias, unlike opinion or anecdote.

points.title: Identifying bioethical issues
points.brief: A bioethical issue arises when biology or medicine raises a question of right and wrong, such as gene editing or cloning.

points.title: Approaches to bioethics
points.brief: Consequences-based, duty-based and virtue-based approaches weigh the same issue in different ways.

points.title: Ethical concepts in biology
points.brief: Integrity, justice, beneficence, non-maleficence and respect guide decisions about bioethical issues.
